skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Automates browser sessions through inference.sh using belt commands, element refs, screenshots, video recording, proxy settings, and form actions.
skill.summary: Control a remote browser with snapshots, element refs, form actions, screenshots, video, and page JavaScript.
skill.author: halt-catch-fire

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown examples, documentation links, or benign shell redirection, and those were marked as false positives. Confirmed risk remains high because the skill enables remote browser automation, screenshots, video recording, authenticated data extraction, arbitrary page JavaScript, file upload, and proxy routing. I found no prompt-injection language in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: Remote screenshots and video can expose sensitive authenticated pages.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent warnings, keep recording disabled by default, redact sensitive pages, and document what data inference.sh receives.

remediation.issue: Proxy documentation includes rate-limit avoidance and anonymity workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Remove rate-limit avoidance examples and limit proxy guidance to authorized geo-testing, corporate access, and compliance-approved testing.

remediation.issue: Authentication documentation shows cookie extraction and output.
remediation.suggestion: Remove cookie-printing examples or replace them with warnings that cookies and session tokens must never be logged or returned to agents.

remediation.issue: The execute function can read sensitive page state.
remediation.suggestion: Document allowed use cases, require explicit user approval before executing page JavaScript, and warn against running it on private sessions.

remediation.issue: Shell templates interpolate user-supplied URLs into JSON inputs.
remediation.suggestion: Build JSON inputs with jq or another structured encoder, validate URLs and output directories, and quote session identifiers consistently.

remediation.issue: File upload workflows can disclose local files.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit file path approval, restrict uploads to intended target domains, and warn users before sending files to a page.

| `screenshot` | Take page screenshot (viewport or full page) |

content.user_title: Automate Browser Workflows With Agent Refs
content.value_statement: Manual browser testing and research slows agents when pages require clicks, forms, or screenshots. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code repeatable browser control through belt, element refs, snapshots, and capture tools.
actual_capabilities: Open browser sessions with custom viewport, user agent, proxy, and video options.
Snapshot pages into compact @e element refs for clicks, fills, selects, drags, and uploads.
Capture viewport screenshots, full-page screenshots, and session videos.
Execute JavaScript in the page context for extraction and inspection.
Provide shell templates for form automation, authenticated sessions, and content capture.
Document proxy, authentication, 2FA, and ref lifecycle workflows.
limitations: Requires the external belt or inference.sh CLI and network access.
Browser activity, screenshots, videos, and page data may pass through a remote service.
Element refs become stale after navigation or DOM changes.
Users must supply credentials, proxy details, and target URLs responsibly.

use_cases.title: Test Interactive Web Flows
use_cases.description: Run login, form, and navigation flows while capturing screenshots or video evidence.

use_cases.title: Collect Web Page Evidence
use_cases.description: Open pages, extract visible text and links, and save screenshots for review.

use_cases.title: Document Browser Workflows
use_cases.description: Record repeatable browser actions with cursor indicators for support or training materials.

prompt_templates.title: Open And Inspect A Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the target page, summarize the title and visible interactive elements, then close the browser session.

prompt_templates.title: Fill A Simple Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the latest snapshot to identify form fields, fill the provided values, submit the form, and report the result.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Research Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Open each approved URL, capture a full-page screenshot, extract visible text and links, and list the saved artifacts.

prompt_templates.title: Automate An Authenticated Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the provided credentials and consented target site to log in, re-snapshot after each navigation, complete the task, and avoid recording sensitive pages.

output_examples.input: Review a public pricing page and capture evidence.
output_examples.output: The page was opened, key navigation elements were listed, a full-page screenshot was captured, and visible pricing text was summarized.

output_examples.input: Test a contact form using provided sample data.
output_examples.output: The form fields were identified from the snapshot, filled with the approved values, submitted, and verified against the final page message.

output_examples.input: Record a short browser workflow for documentation.
output_examples.output: The browser session was recorded with cursor visibility, key steps were completed, and the final video artifact was returned after closing the session.

best_practices: Use only approved target URLs and close every browser session after the task.
Re-snapshot after navigation, form submission, modal changes, or dynamic page updates.
Disable recording and screenshots when credentials or sensitive data are visible.
anti_patterns: Do not use proxy rotation to evade rate limits or site access controls.
Do not print cookies, passwords, TOTP codes, or session tokens in logs.
Do not upload local files unless the target site and file contents are explicitly approved.

faq.question: What does this skill use to control the browser?
faq.answer: It uses the belt or inference.sh CLI with an agent-browser app backed by Playwright.

faq.question: Can it click and fill page elements?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses snapshot output with @e refs for clicks, fills, selects, drags, uploads, and key presses.

faq.question: Can it record browser activity?
faq.answer: Yes. Recording can be enabled when a session opens, and the video is returned when the session closes.

faq.question: Does it support authenticated sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation includes login, OAuth, 2FA, and session reuse patterns.

faq.question: What data risk should users understand?
faq.answer: Screenshots, videos, page text, cookies, and uploaded files can expose sensitive information if used on private pages.

faq.question: Should agents auto-install this skill?
faq.answer: No. Remote browsing, capture, proxies, JavaScript execution, and file uploads require explicit user approval.
